title: He didn’t lose his hand.
paragraphs: He lost his courage to show it.

Because shame doesn’t just wound you…
it teaches you how to hide.
And that’s where the real death begins.
The man in Matthew 12 didn’t just have a shriveled hand.

A part of him stopped working…
and slowly, everything else followed.
And somewhere along the way, he learned the art of concealment.

Keep it behind your back.
Don’t let them see.
Don’t let them know.

Live half a life…
and call it normal.
But on that Sabbath day, everything changed.
Because Jesus walked into the room.
The religious leaders weren’t looking at the man.

“Will He break the rules?”
“Will He heal today?”
They weren’t concerned about the man’s suffering.
They were concerned about their system.

You can be surrounded by people who know Scripture…
and still feel completely unseen.

In front of the eyes that judged him.
In front of the voices that labeled him.

Every insecurity screaming.
Every fear rising.
What if I step forward… and stay broken?
Then Jesus speaks the command that sounds impossible:
That’s the one thing he can’t do.
Because the miracle is not in your ability…
…it’s in your obedience to His word.

“Then He said to the man, ‘Stretch out your hand.’ And the man stretched it out, and it was restored, healthy like the other.”
— Matthew 12:13 (ESV)
The healing didn’t happen before the movement.

At the edge of obedience.
At the risk of exposure.
At the moment he stopped hiding.
Some scholars interpret this as a direct confrontation not only of physical brokenness but of spiritual paralysis—where religion had made people passive, but Jesus calls them into active trust.
Because your “withered hand” might not be visible.
The sin you keep returning to.
The prayer life that dried up.
The addiction you’ve mastered how to hide.
You learned to function around it.
You learned to smile despite it.
You learned to survive with it.

“Don’t bring that to Jesus.”
“You should be better by now.”
“If people knew, they’d walk away.”
You hide the very thing Jesus is asking you to stretch out.
Because this is where everything shifts.
Jesus is not asking you to expose your weakness to humiliate you.
He’s calling it out to heal you.
Sin has withered more than your habits.

“for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God”
— Romans 3:23
At the cross, Jesus stretched out His hands.
Because He took your sin upon Himself.

“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
— Romans 5:8
The same voice that said, “Stretch out your hand”…
is the same voice that says:

“All that the Father gives me will come to me, and whoever comes to me I will never cast out.”
— John 6:37

Not your past.
Not your failure.
Not your secret sin.
Nothing disqualifies you from His mercy—except refusing to come.
So what are you still hiding?
What part of your life have you accepted as permanently broken?
What have you buried under routine, religion, or distraction?
Because healing is waiting on the other side of your obedience.
